newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles controller seeks appeal of FAA order.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles controller seeks appeal of FAA order.

text.p: Los Angeles City Controller Rick Tuttle said on Tuesday the city should appeal a decision by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) demanding that Los Angeles repay $30 million of airport funds.
"I'm urging us to move forward with an appeal," Tuttle said in an interview.

Earlier on Tuesday, a spokesman for the Department of Transportation said the FAA had ordered Los Angeles to return $30.3 million to the Los Angeles Department of Airports because the funds were improperly transferred by the city.

Until the city repays the money, the FAA will freeze $60 million in federal grants for capital improvements at four airports that Los Angeles operates, Department of Transportation spokesman Bill Schulz said.
An investigation by the FAA had determined that the $30.3 million should be "promptly returned to the airport account because it was improperly transferred," he said.
The Los Angeles funds transfer violated a federal law that requires that airport revenues be spent on airport operations, Schulz added.
Tuttle said the airport funds were repayment for past investments by the city for fire safety and certain public works projects at the Los Angeles International Airport.

"I'm not surprised by this (FAA) decision," Tuttle said. "Now I believe we have to move forward in a timely fashion to an administrative law judge. This decision cries out for an appeal to an administrative law judge."

Last November, the Los Angeles City Council voted to hold the funds in a city trust account until the issue was resolved. At the time, City Councilman Nate Holden warned that the council decision could spark a legal battle with the FAA.
